claims.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 310 bps YoY to 14.7% in FY24; standalone EBITDA margin flat at 20.2%
Aspire to restore historical peak EBITDA margin of 32% over next 2-3 years; not expected in FY25
Channel inventory largely cleared; industrial cooling inquiries and orders rising with heat spike
Climate Technologies Australia transitioning to fully outsourced model by Sep'25; portable coolers from India, other products from China; manufacturing footprint contracting
Climate Technologies cost of doing business reduced from ₹77 cr to ₹49 cr in FY24; targeting ~₹38 cr next year
Stock-outs in select models; operations team working to meet unprecedented demand; staggered summer (South then North) helping fulfillment
No formal forward guidance given; aspire to restore historical 32% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years; Climate Technologies targeting revenue recovery to prior levels
Consolidated EBITDA margin doubled to 21% in Q1 FY25 from 9.3% a year ago.
IMPCO Mexico revenue grew 46% YoY to ₹112 crore in Q1 FY25.
GSK China revenue grew from ₹12 crore to ₹16 crore in Q1 FY25.
Climate Technologies Australia revenue declined from ₹51 crore to ₹44 crore in Q1 FY25 due to logistical delays.
Climate Technologies Australia transformation Part 2 progressing as planned; full CODB reduction expected by June 2025 when lease expires.
Management refuses specific quarterly guidance but expects CAGR growth in line with historical trends; June quarter triple-digit growth not a standard.
Demand-supply mismatch left ₹60-80 crore of sales unfulfilled in Q1 FY25; learnings being implemented for future quarters.
Expects respectable double-digit CAGR for India business going forward; believes worst is behind for Australian subsidiary with hockey-stick recovery expected
Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 27.8% from 26.8% due to operating efficiency and economies of scale
Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 840 bps to 20.6% in H1 FY25 driven by better subsidiary realizations and economies of scale
Trade channel inventory below normal at end of summer, supporting strong off-season secondary sales in September quarter
Reclassifying surplus real estate: Thol property (45,000 sqm, market value ~₹61 crore) to investment property; Sindhu Bhavan Road land (1,254 sqm, ~₹30 crore) to assets held-for-sale
China subsidiary developing data center cooling products at development stage; potential commercialization in ~2 years
Management confident about Q4 FY25 performance with spillover of unbilled advances and new margin-accretive models
Record unbilled advances of ₹150 crores as of Dec 31, 2024, primarily for 17 new models
Standalone EBITDA margin 18.8% in Q3; consolidated EBITDA margin 14.7% in Q3; focus on EBITDA margin over gross margin
Consolidated gross margin 50.5% for 9M FY25, up 260 bps YoY
Australia manufacturing to cease by June 2025; lease expiry aligns with manufacturing wind-down
17 new air cooler models; production started Dec/Jan/Feb; spillover from Q3 to Q4
Combined overseas subsidiaries ROCE (EBITDA/Capital Employed) only 1%; core India+China ROCE ~583% on ₹46 crores capital employed
No public ROCE or revenue targets for FY26; internal targets exist but not disclosed per IR policy
No manufacturing plant planned in US; will continue exporting from India and China; trading subsidiary model like Brazil if needed
Climate Technologies Australia expanded into air conditioning, reverse cycle, heating, fans — now addressing AUD 6-7 billion market vs few hundred million earlier
New owners of Climate Technologies Australia and IMPCO Mexico likely to continue sourcing from Symphony India and GSK China due to product fit and retailer continuity
Management does not provide forward-looking numbers for top line, profitability, or margins per IR policy
Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded over 500 bps to 20.05% in FY25; standalone EBITDA margin expanded over 400 bps to 24.25%
Channel inventory is slightly higher than last year at same time but season still has 7-11 weeks remaining in key regions
Consolidated capital employed reduced to ₹248 crores from over ₹300 crores despite revenue growth; standalone capital employed negative ₹32 crores
Production for new models began in January and February; advance placement of inventory in channels ahead of season

Q2 FY26 sales expected to taper vs same quarter last year due to high channel inventory and monsoon season (no consumer sales); channel inventory will normalize only when tertiary sales begin closer to next summer.
Capex for new models (17 launched last year, several in pipeline) only several crores, less than ₹10 cr; asset-light model requires minimal capex to grow.

Symphony AU exited manufacturing (factory lease expired Jul'25, not renewed); fully outsourced from India/China; added salespeople and third-party warehouses across all major Australian cities; now pure sales/marketing/distribution model.
LSV margin significantly better than air coolers; other adjacent products mixed (some higher, some slightly lower).
US major retail chains have shortlisted models, samples sent, finalizing large orders for summer '26.
Channel inventory slightly higher than normal at end of Q2; expected to normalize as season approaches in January-February
Channel inventory at end of September 2025 almost in line with September 2024; sales decline in Q2 automatically adjusted inventory levels
EBITDA margin declined mainly due to operating deleverage; mass product launches impacted product mix
Expanded mass portfolio may impact gross margin by 1-2 percentage points but is accretive at absolute value level
Backend scalability and operational agility built to ramp up production for strong summer seasons
Expect good times ahead; next summer not as bad as 2025, even normal summer should yield strong performance; channel inventory to normalize by season
Trade inventory normalized to levels similar to same period last year after lower primary sales in September quarter
Standalone gross margin 48.3% for 9M; consolidated gross margin ~48% down ~2% YoY for Q3
Consolidated EBITDA ₹24 cr vs ₹35 cr YoY in Q3; 9M EBITDA ₹76 cr vs ₹108 cr
Water heater ad spend ₹11 cr in Q3 (>90% of total A&P); D2C investments already routed through P&L
Accounting treatment for financial investments in rolled-back IB transaction to be determined by auditors as of March 31, 2026 based on past financial performance
Demonstrated ability to more than double production and supply in 60 days during June 2024 bumper summer
Water heater rollout expanded to 8 states covering North and South; general trade added this year; expect higher trajectory over next 2 years
No quantitative FY27 guidance given; management declined to forecast summer growth without weather visibility
Consolidated gross margin 46.4% in Q4 FY26, flat YoY; EBITDA margin 15.5% vs 21.2% due to operating leverage; standalone gross margin ~45%, EBITDA margin 17% vs 27%
BISP portfolio contributed ₹558 cr (49% of FY26 consolidated revenue); standalone BISP revenue ₹192 cr (25% of ₹765 cr)
No further capital allocation to Australia; ₹52 cr remitted to acquire US equity and IPRs; Australia monthly CODB ~₹5-6 cr to reduce further
Australia shifting to distributor model; warehousing to be eliminated; monthly CODB ~₹5-6 cr to reduce further
Expect margin pressure in short term due to elevated costs from war; will pass on some but not all cost increases
Expect significant growth in Mexico for summer of FY27 after two consecutive mild summers
Expect GSK China to continue momentum; Bonaire USA current quarter good but subsequent quarters muted due to seasonality
Consolidated gross margin 49.8% and EBITDA margin 12.6% in Q1 FY27; margins marginally increased despite headwinds
Price hikes of 7-10% taken in non-household cooler segments; household segment hikes pending
BISP (Beyond India Summer Products) contributed ₹560 crore (48% of consolidated TTM revenue) and ₹179 crore (23% of standalone TTM revenue)
No further capital allocation to CTPL Australia; impairment and write-off completed in FY26
Bonaire USA revenue grew 35% driven by successful scale-up of Air Force model (rebranded Indian SKU) and strong US Southwest summer
GSK China revenue grew 43%; now completely debt free after repaying all debt and interest to Symphony India
Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue ₹275 cr vs ₹210 cr, up 31%; EBITDA ₹36 cr vs ₹13 cr; PAT ₹24 cr vs ₹17 cr
Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue ₹653 cr up 17%; EBITDA ₹83 cr vs ₹51 cr; PAT ₹64 cr vs ₹59 cr
Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue ₹170 cr vs ₹155 cr; EBITDA ₹30 cr vs ₹27 cr; PAT ₹29 cr
Standalone H1 FY27 revenue ₹411 cr vs ₹384 cr; PAT ₹57 cr vs ₹65 cr but business PAT higher
Consolidated EBITDA margin 13% vs 6.4% despite gross margin down ~4% due to operating leverage and cost discipline
Standalone gross margin down ~2.3% but EBITDA margin almost maintained
Standalone H1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.4%, up 18% YoY; expect next two quarters somewhat better
New products (RAC, BLDC fans, air purifiers) zero capex for ACs and fans; purifier may need small capex later
IMPCO Mexico Q2 revenue ₹40 cr vs ₹17 cr; GSK China ₹23 cr; Australia+USA ₹46 cr vs ₹35 cr
New products outsourced; BLDC fan partner finalized, rollout soon; RAC sourced from China for exports
No specific revenue targets for new categories; baby steps, EBITDA-accretive, no delusions of grandeur
No ad spend or launch OPEX in current quarter; measured brand investment may come summer
